newsitem.title: USA: NYC union says reaches no-layoff pact with MTA.
newsitem.headline: NYC union says reaches no-layoff pact with MTA.

text.p: The New York City subway and bus workers union said Wednesday it has a no-layoff preliminary pact with the New York State Metropolitan Transportation Authority, which has said it needed to cut costs to avoid layoffs and a fare hike.

Willie James, the president of Transport Workers Union Local 100, said, "My members have been deeply concerned about privatization and the possibility of layoffs for the past year. This contract addresses those fears," in prepared remarks.
The union represents more that 30,000 hourly paid employees at the Transit Authority and the Manhattan and Bronx Surface Operating Authority.
However, the state agency, which oversees the Transit Authority that runs New York City's subway, commuter railroads and bus lines, still has not given its final approval, according to the union.
"They really haven't bounced this off the executive board," said a union spokesman.
A spokesman for the Metropolitan Transportation Authority was not immediately available to comment on the pact the union said it had agreed.

Earlier, he said that the agency was seeking to cut costs by as much as $350 million in the last three years of the agency's five-year fiscal plan, but he added that the Transit Authority might not be the only agency in this cost-cutting drive.

The union's contract has another year to run but the agency spokesman said the union picked up the pace of the talks after the agency sent a letter to the president of the Transit Authority asking him to identify savings.
The president of the union said he planned to release the details of the new contract Thursday morning.
